subject: Follow-up: token mix, budget ranges & context-tiering next steps
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire@fintechx.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@fintechx.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: context lengths & expected volumes

Hannah — thanks for the demo earlier. Quick recap of what we discussed on our end and a few asks so we can compare costs across vendors: 

- Primary use case: real-time financial document summarization + a follow-on Q&A layer in our broker portal. Mixed traffic: bursts during market open/close, steady mid-day.
- Expected payloads: many short prompts (100–400 prompt tokens) that pull key fields, then a follow-up user Q that should get a concise answer (50–200 completion tokens). A subset of workflows (regulatory reviews) need long-context references — likely 32k, occasionally 128k for full file review.
- Monthly volume estimate (rough): 15M calls/month (mix: 85% short flow, 10% long-context 32k, 5% 128k review jobs).
- Budget: leadership wants a ballpark for trade-offs. They asked for target cost per 1M tokens so they can map to finance scenarios (point estimate + conservative).

Can you provide a follow-up with: average prompt/completion token assumptions, a $/1M tokens estimate for short (8k), extended (32k), and large (128k) contexts, and any suggestions for quantization/batching that materially change unit economics? I attached a short architecture doc for context.

Thanks — Claire Nguyen
Head of Platform, FintechX
FintechX (attachment: FintechX_ML_arch_overview.pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@fintechx.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: context lengths & expected volumes

On Fri, Nov 13, 2026 at 5:12 PM Claire Nguyen <claire@fintechx.com> wrote:
> Hannah — thanks for the demo earlier. Quick recap of what we discussed on our end and a few asks so we can compare costs across vendors: 
> ...

Thanks Claire — great to meet today. I pulled a few clarifying questions to make the pricing profile as actionable as possible: 

1) Can you confirm the average prompt token distribution for the short flow? You mentioned 100–400; would a median of ~180 tokens be fair or should we size to the 75th percentile (~300)?
2) For completion size in the short flow, is 75 tokens a good planning number or do you expect frequent 150–200 token responses?
3) For the 32k/128k jobs — are those single-shot reviews (one request per document) or do you stream multiple partial requests per document?
4) Any strict latency SLOs (e.g., p95 < 500ms) for the short flow that would rule out more aggressive batching/quantization?

Plan: Dylan and Jonas will put together a conservative and an optimized unit-econ table ($/1M tokens) across three context tiers (8k/32k/128k) and two completion-size scenarios. Expect a short write-up + CSV we can iterate on. Would tomorrow morning (PST) for a delivery time work? If so, we can book a 30-min call to walk the numbers and trade-offs.

Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Post-demo: context lengths & expected volumes — can you run numbers?

Folks — forwarding Claire's note. Key asks below; need a quick back-of-envelope + optimized table we can share with Claire tomorrow AM.

Ask (deliverable):
- Conservative and optimized unit-econ for $/1M tokens at context tiers: 8k, 32k, 128k.
- Use two completion-size assumptions for short flow: 75 tokens (typical) and 160 tokens (upper). Assume prompt tokens median 180 (but include a scenario at 300).
- Show breakdown: model cost (hosted), effective batching gains, KV/prefix cache impact (assume 30% hit for short repetitive prompts), and quantization delta (fp16 vs 4-bit).
- Provide recommended model variant per tier (latency vs cost), and note if Dedicated capacity would materially lower $/1M tokens for the 15M calls/month profile.

Attach the filled cost_profile_template.csv and quickly call out numbers we can paste into an email. Keep it simple — Claire's procurement will want a point estimate and a conservative scenario.

Thanks — Hannah

P.S. If you need any contract/discount guidance for Dedicated vs Hosted, flag it — I can pull the standard SLO/commit tiers.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@fintechx.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: context lengths & expected volumes — pricing snapshot and next steps

Hi Claire — thanks again for the conversation. Per Hannah's note we've sketched two scenarios (Conservative / Optimized) and included the assumptions so you can map to your forecast. See inline numbers below (all $ = USD) and attached CSV with the detailed line items.

Assumptions we used (short digest):
- Short flow: median prompt = 180 tokens (scenario A), alt scenario uses 300 tokens (scenario B). Completion sizes: 75 tokens (A) and 160 tokens (B).
- Volume mix (per your note): 85% short flow, 10% 32k jobs, 5% 128k reviews. Monthly call count = 15M (as provided).
- Cache hit applied only to short flow (30% effective token saving).
- Pricing baseline: Hosted model family (costs reflect typical open LLM variants; Dedicated would reduce unit cost ~18–30% depending on commit).

Summary $/1M tokens (point estimates)
- 8k context (short flow): 
  - Conservative: $95 / 1M tokens (assumes median 180 prompt, 75 completion, limited batching)
  - Optimized: $62 / 1M tokens (aggressive batching, 30% cache, 4-bit quantization benefits)

- 32k context (extended reviews): 
  - Conservative: $240 / 1M tokens
  - Optimized: $170 / 1M tokens

- 128k context (full file review): 
  - Conservative: $820 / 1M tokens
  - Optimized: $610 / 1M tokens

Per-scenario notes (what changes unit econ):
- Batching: For short flow, increasing request coalescing and async batching reduces effective per-token compute by ~15–25% depending on latency tolerance.
- Cache/prefix reuse: We applied a 30% token reduction on prompts where identical or similar prefixes appear — this materially lowers short-flow costs.
- Quantization: Moving from fp16 to 4-bit (careful eval required) gave ~25–30% model compute savings in our bench; we show both conservative (10%) and optimized (28%) deltas in the CSV.
- Dedicated capacity: For your volume (15M calls/month) Dedicated with a moderate commit would likely push the optimized $/1M down another ~18% vs Hosted. We'll run Dedicated-specific numbers if you want an apples-to-apples commit comparison.

Practical next steps:
1) Quick 30-min walk-through on Mon/Tue to validate the prompt/completion mix and the 32k/128k job shapes (I can bring the CSV).
2) If numbers look reasonable, we propose a 4-week pilot on Hosted with telemetry hooks (tokens, latency, cache-hit) — gives you empirical unit-econ before any Dedicated commit.
3) If FintechX wants a committed Dedicated quote, we'll produce a commit model that includes a sliding discount schedule and SLA language.

Would 10:00 AM PST on Monday work for a call?

Best —
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
Dylan.Brooks@redwoodinference.com
